final_answer: Fix `wait_state_stuck` by adding a single inline predicate to `Get-SynthesisDepthDecision` in `lib/decision-depth.ps1` that recognizes generic plan-refinement/DISCUSS backlog tasks, and use that predicate to gate exactly the two escalation branches that misfire: the keyword-only High-Stakes domain escalation (Step 2) and the generic DISCUSS→Deep escalation (Step 3). The predicate must match plan-refinement/atom-list terms AND artifact terms together (e.g. `plan.?refin|refine|refinement|уточн|доработ` AND `atom|backlog|plan|план|spec|self.?improve`) so that incidental high-stakes keywords or a bare 'discuss' in a routine backlog/atom task route Standard instead of High-Stakes or Deep. Explicit `[[HIGH-STAKES]]` markers and explicit `risk in {high,critical}` remain hard overrides that bypass the predicate, and genuine architecture/design discussions still route Deep because the predicate requires co-occurring artifact terms it will not match. The production change is confined to `lib/decision-depth.ps1` with no new functions, files, or router layers (reuse `$low` and existing flow); regression assertions are added to the existing harness `tools/test-decision-synthesis.ps1`, which is the only permitted secondary edit. All seven atoms scored high (0.74–0.95) with no conflicts and no micro-debate, so all are accepted — three with the judge's modifications folded in (ATOM_001 scope, ATOM_002 predicate narrowing, ATOM_007 testing).

decisions.decision: Confine the production change to an inline predicate inside `Get-SynthesisDepthDecision` in `lib/decision-depth.ps1`; reuse existing variables (e.g. `$low`); add no new helpers, files, or router layers; preserve the depth result space (Simple|Standard|Deep|High-Stakes). Permit test-only edits to `tools/test-decision-synthesis.ps1` as the single allowed secondary file.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies the reuse-only / atomic-single-edit constraint while resolving the judge's flagged conflict between ATOM_001's single-file rule and ATOM_007's need to add assertions: the production logic stays in one file and one edit, and the harness file is touched only to add regression coverage, which the task's own output_format ('updated or new test cases') anticipates.

Strictly one file with zero test changes

decisions.decision: Introduce a single inline predicate (e.g. `$isPlanRefinementDiscussTask`) that is true only when text matches plan-refinement/atom-list terms (`plan.?refin|refine|refinement|уточн|доработ`) AND artifact terms (`atom|backlog|plan|план|spec|self.?improve`), using word boundaries and validated against a corpus so it does not over-match architecture/design planning.
decisions.rationale: The conjunction (refinement-term AND artifact-term) is what distinguishes routine backlog/atom-list churn from genuine deliberation. A bare `refine` or `plan` token would over-match real architecture/design planning and wrongly de-escalate it; requiring artifact terms keeps the predicate specific, which the judge required as the condition for ATOM_002 and ATOM_006 to hold.

Hard-coded list of exact task titles

decisions.decision: Gate the keyword-only High-Stakes domain escalation branch (Step 2) with the new predicate, so plan-refinement/DISCUSS tasks carrying incidental high-stakes keywords do not escalate to High-Stakes.
decisions.rationale: This is the direct cause of `wait_state_stuck`: incidental domain keywords in routine refinement tasks trigger the heaviest route. Gating only the keyword-only branch removes the false escalation while leaving explicit-risk and small-task logic intact (composition, not replacement, per the judge).

decisions.decision: Preserve explicit High-Stakes escalation: `[[HIGH-STAKES]]` markers and `$riskVal -in @('high','critical')` continue to force High-Stakes, overriding the new predicate.
decisions.rationale: Highest-scored atom (0.9495). Explicit markers and declared high/critical risk are intentional safety signals and must remain hard overrides; the predicate only suppresses keyword-only and generic-discuss escalation, never explicit ones.

red_team_findings.what: The fix gates the depth CLASSIFIER, but routing-into-synthesis for DISCUSS tasks is decided by an independent $ExplicitDiscuss flag that has PRECEDENCE over $depth. In Get-SynthesisRouteDecision (lib/decision-depth.ps1:189-191) the order is: elseif ($ExplicitDeepThink){route} / elseif ($ExplicitDiscuss){route=true} / elseif ($depth -in @('Deep','High-Stakes')){route}. The driver computes the discuss marker itself from the same task text: backlog path driver/81-loop-idle-claim.ps1:1574 ($backlogDiscussMark via '\bdiscuss\b|обсуди|...') and idle path :358 ($discussVerbMark). The target class is literally 'plan-refinement/DISCUSS' — these tasks contain the word 'discuss'/'обсуди' — so $ExplicitDiscuss=true forces route=true REGARDLESS of the gated depth.
red_team_findings.why: Defeats success_test #1 ('wait_state_stuck no longer occurs under the specific triggering scenario') and #2. Dropping depth to Standard does NOT remove a discuss-containing task from synthesis, contradicting the decision's load-bearing premise (proposal_B: 'Standard ⇒ not in synthesis'). The bypass lives in driver/81-loop-idle-claim.ps1, which the 'changes confined to lib/decision-depth.ps1' constraint forbids touching — so the fix as scoped CANNOT resolve the bug for the named task class.

red_team_findings.what: The chosen test altitude is structurally blind to the bypass above. Per ATOM_002/ATOM_009 (the dependency decision dec-...-1192ef) and the test as landed (tools/test-decision-synthesis.ps1:169-171), assertions call Get-SynthesisDepthDecision DIRECTLY and explicitly NOT Get-SynthesisRouteDecision/Invoke-SynthesisPipeline. So the regression test will be green (classifier returns Standard) while production still routes into synthesis via $ExplicitDiscuss.
red_team_findings.why: Creates a false-green: the suite passing is presented as evidence that wait_state_stuck is fixed, but no test exercises the actual routing path that wedges. success_test 'wait_state_stuck no longer occurs' is asserted by a harness that cannot observe the failure mode.

red_team_findings.what: Even on the path the fix does control, the fix is mostly a no-op or an over-correction. (a) Pure 'refine'-only tasks already return Standard pre-fix: 'refine/refinement/уточн/доработ' appear in NO escalation regex (not in Step-2 $highStakesKw at line 81, not in the Step-3 regex at line 89), so they never reached Deep/High-Stakes to begin with. (b) The cases the fix actually changes are tasks hitting Step-3 terms NOT in the driver's discuss list (e.g. 'approach','strategy','подход','страте') AND matching the predicate — a narrow band that largely excludes the architecture terms ATOM_006 wants preserved.
red_team_findings.why: The headline goal ('generic refine/discuss terms no longer escalate') is addressed for a set that is either already-correct (refine-only) or bypassed (discuss-containing). The genuine effective domain is small and does not include the named symptom, so the behavioral payoff is far smaller than the record claims.

red_team_findings.what: The $isPlanRefinement predicate over-matches via unanchored substring regex, broadly suppressing legitimate High-Stakes escalation. Artifact term 'plan' matches inside 'control-plane' and 'plane'/'explanation'; 'spec' matches 'specification/inspect/especially'; and 'atom|backlog|self.?improve' match essentially EVERY self-improvement backlog auto-task (their IDs are 'ATOM_xxx', they come from the backlog, they are 'self-improve'). So for the backlog class the artifact half is ~always true, reducing the predicate to 'contains a refine word'. Combined: a long self-improve backlog task touching payment/security/control-plane/irreversible that also says 'refine' gets the Step-2 keyword High-Stakes branch suppressed.
red_team_findings.why: The backlog call site (driver/81-loop-idle-claim.ps1:1575) passes NO -Intent and NO -Risk, so $riskVal is empty and [[HIGH-STAKES]] literal is the ONLY surviving High-Stakes signal for these tasks. Gating the keyword branch therefore silently de-escalates genuinely high-stakes control-plane backlog work to Standard — exactly the under-routing the 2026-06-19 $isSmallTask author warned about (lib/decision-depth.ps1:71-77). This is a real safety regression, not a flagged-and-accepted edge.

red_team_findings.what: Step-2 gate-placement trap. Step 2's condition is `$riskVal -in @('high','critical') -or ($highStakesKw -and -not $isSmallTask)` (lib/decision-depth.ps1:82). The decision says keep risk=high authoritative, but if the implementer wraps the whole `if` with `-and -not $isPlanRefinement` (the literal 'gate the branch' instruction), it ALSO suppresses the explicit risk=high path — violating ATOM_004. Only the keyword sub-clause may be gated. The existing tests have NO non-marker risk=high case (only the [[HIGH-STAKES]] literal at line 174), and ATOM_007's list writes it as '[[HIGH-STAKES]] (or risk=high)', permitting the author to test only the marker.
red_team_findings.why: A plausible misimplementation breaks the most authoritative atom (ATOM_004, score 0.937) and would escape the test suite — directly threatening success_test 'explicit high-risk tasks still route High-Stakes' while the suite reports PASS.

red_team_findings.what: Vacuous-regression risk from the unmentioned $isSmallTask guard. The landed ATOM_003 standardText ('Plan refinement request: adjust backlog atom ordering...') already returns Standard on UNMODIFIED code (no escalation trigger present), so it does not gate the fix. Worse, the planned ATOM_004 case 'high-stakes-keyword-quoting plan-refinement → Standard' also returns Standard pre-fix when short, because Step-2 requires `-not $isSmallTask` and $isSmallTask is true for any text < 160 chars (line 80). The decision's open_questions never mention $isSmallTask.
red_team_findings.why: An implementer following the plan literally can write a regression test that is green both before and after the change, satisfying 'a new ATOM_004 test passes' in letter while proving nothing. To be non-vacuous the keyword case must be deliberately crafted >160 chars and non-trivial complexity — a constraint absent from the record.

red_team_findings.what: Diagnosis/contract mismatch on the word 'High-Stakes'. The task goal and success_test #2 assert 'generic refine/discuss phrases escalate to High-Stakes', but no such path exists: 'refine' is in no escalation regex, and 'discuss' routes to Deep (Step 3 → line 90), not High-Stakes. High-Stakes is reachable only via the [[HIGH-STAKES]] literal, $riskVal, or domain keywords ($highStakesKw) — none of which are the literal words 'refine'/'discuss'.
red_team_findings.why: A success_test phrased as 'a task containing the word refine does not escalate to High-Stakes' passes vacuously pre- and post-fix, giving misleading verification credit. The real over-routing is discuss→Deep and domain-keyword→High-Stakes; the contract's framing can cause the wrong assertion to be written.
